Same earnings report: two hours if you grind through it yourself, ten minutes with these 4 steps.

The difference isn't that AI is smarter than you - it's whether you spelled out what to ask before hitting enter. Most people paste "summarise this earnings report" and get back a summary anyone could have written.

Copy these 4 steps:

1. Download the actual filing or earnings deck from the company's investor relations page (or your market's official disclosure site). Give the AI the source document - never let it answer from memory.
2. Upload the file and paste the prompt below.
3. Check every cell it returns against the original, by page number. Anything you can't verify, delete.
4. Save it as your own tracking sheet. Next quarter, run the same 4 steps and only look at what changed.

The prompt (copy it):
"The file I uploaded is this company's latest quarterly report. Answer using only what appears in the file. If something isn't there, write 'not stated in the document' - do not use numbers from memory. Give me a table with five rows: (1) the change in revenue and profit this quarter, plus the company's own explanation, quoting the original sentence; (2) any item in gross margin or cost structure that moved in the opposite direction from last quarter; (3) what management said about next quarter, labelled as a commitment, an estimate, or vague language; (4) the one risk in this document most readers would skim past, with the page number; (5) the three numbers I should track next quarter to know whether this story is going off course. Finish with a three-sentence summary. Do not give price levels or buy/sell calls - facts and risk logic only."

Why it works: keeping it inside the file blocks the most common failure - stale numbers stated with total confidence. Page numbers make it checkable. Labelling guidance as commitment / estimate / vague turns PR language into something you can track.

Warning: what comes out is a checklist to verify, not a conclusion. Re-check every number against the source yourself.
